biomarkers.name: HPV DNA / RNA (p16 IHC as surrogate)
biomarkers.prevalence: Oncogenic HPV drives this entity, most commonly HPV-16. HPV positivity and p16 positivity are not perfectly concordant; '100% p16+' is true only for a cohort defined by p16 positivity, not for every transcriptionally active HPV-associated tumor.
biomarkers.clinical_use: Defines the HPV-associated entity; p16 IHC is the accepted surrogate for AJCC 8 separate oropharyngeal staging, with positivity defined by moderate-to-strong nuclear and cytoplasmic staining in at least 70% of tumor cells. HPV-specific testing is indicated in selected settings, including discordant morphology and p16 results. E6/E7 RNA testing demonstrates transcriptionally active HPV; HPV DNA detection alone does not necessarily establish viral causation. HPV-associated disease generally has a better prognosis and is the subject of de-intensification trials, but HPV/p16 positivity alone does not justify treatment de-intensification outside an appropriate clinical trial.

biomarkers.name: Plasma ctDNA HPV (TTMV-HPV DNA)
biomarkers.prevalence: n/a (assay); circulating HPV DNA is not detectable in every patient with HPV-associated disease.
biomarkers.clinical_use: Emerging use for surveillance and detection of molecular residual disease; commercial assays such as NavDx are available. TTMV-HPV DNA is a specific circulating HPV DNA assay approach, not a synonym for all plasma HPV ctDNA assays. Optimal testing schedules and management of positive results remain under investigation; a survival benefit from assay-guided surveillance has not been established. Testing does not replace standard clinical evaluation, imaging, or pathological confirmation of suspected recurrence when feasible.

biomarkers.name: PD-L1 (CPS)
biomarkers.prevalence: Variable; positivity depends on the assay, CPS threshold, and cohort and is not defined by HPV status.
biomarkers.clinical_use: As for HPV-negative recurrent/metastatic HNSCC, PD-L1 CPS guides first-line pembrolizumab monotherapy eligibility: CPS at least 1 under the US FDA indication. Pembrolizumab plus platinum and fluorouracil is a first-line option regardless of CPS. HPV positivity alone is not a substitute for PD-L1 testing or a validated standalone predictor of PD-1 inhibitor benefit.

biomarkers.name: E6 / E7 oncoproteins
biomarkers.prevalence: Expression of high-risk HPV E6/E7 is the hallmark viral driver mechanism; this does not mean that E6/E7 proteins are routinely measured or detected in every diagnostic specimen.
biomarkers.clinical_use: E6 promotes p53 degradation, and E7 inactivates the RB pathway, producing characteristic p16 overexpression. Detection of E6/E7 RNA supports transcriptionally active HPV infection; direct oncoprotein testing is not a routine standalone diagnostic standard. E6/E7 are therapeutic vaccine targets in clinical trials. No recurrent host-gene mutation or driver fusion is required to define this entity.

histomorphological_subtype.primary_pattern: Usually non-keratinizing SCC with basaloid features, often with a lymphoepithelioma-like appearance; morphology alone does not establish HPV association.
variants: keratinizing variant (recognized in HPV-associated disease; an independently worse prognosis is not established sufficiently for routine prognostic classification)
adenosquamous (rare; HPV association requires appropriate testing)
histomorphological_subtype.grading: Conventional differentiation-based SCC grading is not recommended for HPV-associated oropharyngeal SCC. Its immature-appearing morphology should not automatically be interpreted as biologically poorly differentiated disease. AJCC 8 introduced separate p16-based staging.

tumor_microenvironment.immune_context: Frequently immune-inflamed or 'hot', with dense tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes and a distinctive immune signature, but substantial intertumoral heterogeneity exists.
tumor_microenvironment.stromal_features: Often rich in lymphocytes, sometimes producing a lymphoepithelioma-like appearance; adjacent tonsillar lymphoid tissue also contributes to this appearance.

cellular_states_and_lineage.cell_of_origin: Thought to arise predominantly from the reticulated epithelium of palatine or lingual tonsillar crypts, a specialized permeable epithelium closely associated with lymphoid tissue; the precise initiating cell population is not definitively established.
cellular_states_and_lineage.developmental_lineage: Generally attributed to pharyngeal endodermal epithelium; palatine tonsillar epithelium derives from the second pharyngeal pouch, rather than pharyngeal arch mesenchyme.
cellular_states_and_lineage.differentiation_state: Usually non-keratinizing squamous, with immature-appearing basaloid morphology. Minimal keratinization is characteristic but not defining, because keratinizing HPV-associated tumors occur; this appearance is not equivalent to conventional poor differentiation.
cellular_states_and_lineage.lineage_plasticity: HPV E6/E7 disrupt cell-cycle control and support cellular immortalization and malignant transformation. These effects do not themselves establish a specific lineage-plasticity program. Crypt epithelial architecture and sometimes discohesive growth may facilitate early access to lymphatics; frequent nodal spread can coexist with a favorable prognosis, but discohesion alone is not an established explanation.
